protocol: Extend the abdominal examination to the lung bases, pleura, pericardium (subxiphoid window) and the chest wall at the site of maximal tenderness, using curvilinear and high-frequency probes.

checklist.label: Lung bases
checklist.detail: Look above each hemidiaphragm for consolidation with air bronchograms.

checklist.label: Pleura
checklist.detail: Assess pleural fluid, its echogenicity and lung sliding.

checklist.detail: Look for pleural-based hypoechoic lesions that may represent infarcts in suspected pulmonary embolism.

checklist.detail: Examine the point of maximal tenderness for cortical discontinuity and haematoma.

measurements.name: Fluid depth
measurements.method: Measure the maximal perpendicular depth of pleural or pericardial fluid and state the patient position.
measurements.pitfall: Depth is not volume; report position and distribution.

measurements.name: Lesion size
measurements.method: Measure the largest dimension of a consolidation or peripheral lung lesion in two planes.
measurements.pitfall: Only the pleural-based portion of a lesion is visible.

pitfalls: A normal thoracic ultrasound does not exclude central pneumonia or central pulmonary embolism; CT pulmonary angiography remains the test for embolism.
Pleural-based hypoechoic lesions are not specific; interpret them with the clinical probability of pulmonary embolism.
impression_prompts: Is there a thoracic cause — consolidation, pleural or pericardial fluid, a peripheral lung lesion or a rib fracture — at the site of pain?
Is further imaging, such as CT pulmonary angiography or chest radiography, needed?
Which abdominal causes remain unexcluded?
escalation: Immediately communicate features of cardiac tamponade or a large pericardial effusion; communicate lesions suggesting pulmonary embolism promptly.

protocol: Use contrast-enhanced CT or MR angiography timed to the vessels in question, with multiplanar and 3D reconstructions of the arch, pulmonary arteries and veins.
Record symptoms of airway or oesophageal compression, prior surgery and whether the question is arterial, venous or shunt-related.

checklist.label: Aortic arch
checklist.detail: Establish arch side, branching order, aberrant subclavian artery, diverticulum, double arch and coarctation.

checklist.label: Airway and oesophagus
checklist.detail: Look for a vascular ring or sling compressing the trachea or oesophagus.

checklist.label: Pulmonary arteries
checklist.detail: Assess pulmonary artery origin and course, agenesis, sling and ductus arteriosus.

checklist.label: Pulmonary veins
checklist.detail: Trace every pulmonary vein to its drainage site and look for anomalous return.

checklist.label: Systemic veins
checklist.detail: Identify a left superior vena cava, azygos continuation of the IVC and the left superior intercostal vein.

measurements.name: Vessel calibre
measurements.method: Measure the minimum orthogonal diameter at named segments, such as a coarctation and the adjacent normal aorta.
measurements.pitfall: Oblique axial measurements overestimate calibre; use a plane perpendicular to the vessel.

measurements.name: Airway narrowing
measurements.method: Measure the minimum tracheal or bronchial lumen at the level of compression and its length.
measurements.pitfall: Expiratory phase and patient position change airway calibre.

pitfalls: A right arch with an aberrant left subclavian artery and a diverticulum can form a complete vascular ring through the ligamentum arteriosum, which CT does not show directly.
A single contrast phase may under-opacify an anomalous vein; review delayed images before calling a vein absent.
impression_prompts: What is the vascular anomaly and does it form a ring or sling?
Is the trachea or oesophagus compressed, and where?
Are there associated pulmonary venous or systemic venous anomalies or a shunt?
escalation: Communicate critical airway compression or a severe coarctation promptly.
